questions.prompt: You're pasting a 40-page report and asking one question about it. Where should the question go?

options.text: At the very top, before the report
In the middle of the report
At the end, after the report

questions.explanation: For long inputs, put documents first and the question last. Anthropic reports up to 30 percent better quality in its tests, and Google's guide gives the same advice.

questions.prompt: Which of these are elements of a prompt? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Role, context, input data, examples, instruction, rules, tone, and output format are prompt elements. The training cutoff is a property of the model, not something you write.

questions.prompt: A reusable prompt with placeholders for the parts that change is called a prompt ____.
questions.explanation: Templates turn a working prompt into something you can fill with new inputs and test consistently.

questions.prompt: Order the letters of C.R.E.A.T.E. by what they stand for.
questions.explanation: C.R.E.A.T.E. is Context, Role, Examples, Action, Tone, Experiment, from Mark Austin's book.

questions.prompt: A prompt says: Summarize this email. Dear team please make a list of everyone who must approve... What's the main problem?

options.text: Instructions and data are tangled, so the model may follow the email's request instead of summarizing
Summaries are not a supported task
It should be in all capital letters

questions.explanation: Without delimiters, the model can't tell where your instruction ends and the email begins. Wrap the email in tags and keep your instruction outside them.

questions.prompt: Match each element to an example of it.

pairs.right: You are an experienced pediatric nurse.
Parents will read this at home after a clinic visit.
Use words a 12-year-old knows. Max 8 items.
A numbered list, then one sentence on when to call a doctor.

questions.explanation: Role sets expertise and voice, context supplies background, rules limit what's allowed, and format sets the shape of the answer.
